name: roswell
desc: Lisp installer and launcher for major environments
why: A Common Lisp installer and launcher that gives a door into the Lisp implementation zoo, a close call on the plumbing side.

brief.what_it_is: Roswell is a command-line tool for installing, switching between, and launching Common Lisp implementations, and it has grown into a broader development environment. You run the single `ros` executable with git-style subcommands such as install, use, run, init, build, and list. It can fetch prebuilt implementations (the README names sbcl-bin and ccl-bin), install Quicklisp libraries or GitHub-hosted scripts, and create and build executable Lisp scripts. The README also describes Roswell as an environment for testing, sharing, and distributing Lisp applications.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says the aim was to make installing and managing Common Lisp implementations 'really simple and easy', and the broader goal is to 'push the Common Lisp community to a whole new level of productivity'. The naming section frames making Lisp easier to use as a way for people to 'mingle with alien technology'.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives no internals. It describes a git-like command interface modelled on cl-launch and buildapp, with `ros [options] [[--] script-path arguments...]` as the other invocation form. Scripts are plain files with a `#!/bin/sh` header that runs `exec ros -Q -- $0 "$@"`, so the Lisp file is executed through Roswell.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew is one route. The README points to a GitHub wiki for installation on Linux, FreeBSD, macOS via Homebrew, Windows, and building from source. Prebuilt binaries are provided for Homebrew on macOS, various Linux distributions, and Windows. On first use Roswell downloads the default stable implementation (sbcl-bin) unless you first run `ros lisp=sbcl-bin/system setup` to use a system Lisp. Fetching wiki pages was not in scope, so exact per-platform steps are not verified here.
brief.standout: It bundles an implementation manager with script running and building, which the README says are similar to cl-launch and buildapp, and adds a scaffold command (`ros init`) and a way to install scripts from Quicklisp or GitHub. The README also lists Bash completion and CI integration (Travis, CircleCI, Coveralls) as features.
brief.status: Maintained, judging by the GitHub releases page: the latest release is v26.10.118, with assets dated 12 Oct, and there are multiple releases in 2026 following a steady cadence since 2021. I did not check the commit history, and the README gives no abandonment note.
brief.caveats: The README says Roswell 'is still in beta', though it adds that 'the basic interfaces are stable and not likely to change'. It works well on Unix-like systems such as Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD. On other operating systems 'some parts or features might be missing or unstable'. The README links to an issues list for known gaps. The Windows claim 'tested exhaustively' is the author's own wording. The license is MIT.
quotes: Roswell is a Lisp implementation installer/manager, launcher, and much more!
Roswell is still in beta. Despite this, the basic interfaces are stable and not likely to change.
Roswell has git-like subcommands which resemble that of cl-launch, buildapp.
